artist.name: Astrid S
artist.short_description: Norwegian pop singer-songwriter whose catalogue pairs relationship-focused writing with polished pop and electronic influences.
artist.biography: Astrid S is the recording name of Astrid Smeplass, a Norwegian singer and songwriter from Berkåk in the Rennebu area. She received piano and singing tuition while growing up, and also learned flute and guitar. Her wider public breakthrough came after finishing fifth on Norway’s Idol in 2013; she subsequently signed with Universal Music. The self-titled Astrid S EP arrived in 2016 and included Hurts So Good, which became one of her signature releases. Party’s Over followed in 2017, a period that also brought Breathe, Such A Boy and Think Before I Talk. She earned a Norwegian Spellemann newcomer prize for 2016 and the Artist of the Year honor for 2017. Her debut studio album, Leave It Beautiful, appeared in October 2020. Her official biography frames the album as personal writing shaped by breakups, major changes and the experience of growing up; It’s Ok If You Forget Me is one of its key songs. Her second studio album, Joyride, followed in May 2024. In a contemporary interview, she compared the title track’s fleeting romance with her approach to enjoying life without dwelling on uncertain outcomes. Across these releases, her documented pop background sits alongside electronic and R&B influences, while the emotional range stretches from argument and regret to infatuation and acceptance. For Afterglow, the attraction is the contrast between accessible pop songwriting and emotionally complicated stories; that final characterization is editorial, not an official genre designation.

artist.short_description: North Carolina-born, Nashville-based singer-songwriter making personal, emotionally direct folk-pop and singer-songwriter pop.
artist.biography: Caleb Hearn is an American singer-songwriter from Mount Airy, North Carolina, who is based in Nashville, Tennessee. Growing up around family members who made music, he learned guitar as a child and developed an interest in writing songs. During the COVID-19 period, he reconsidered his direction as a musician, turning toward more personal material rather than chasing a particular commercial sound. His reworked 2020 release “Always Be 2.0,” drawn from grief after the death of a close friend, became a breakthrough with listeners online. In 2022, Hearn signed with Nettwerk and released “Where Do We Go from Here?,” a story inspired by a family he knew. His 2022 EP We’re Getting Older examined heartbreak and the effort to understand himself; 2023’s 1200 sq ft looked back at childhood and family life. His duet “Little Bit Better” with ROSIE arrived in 2024 and became one of his best-known recordings. That year also brought his debut studio album, Left on McKinney. In February 2026, he followed it with LEAVE THE WORLD BEHIND, a second album reflecting on change and moving forward. For Afterglow listeners, Hearn fits the intersection of confessional pop, folk-pop, and intimate singer-songwriter storytelling. That genre description is editorial, informed by published descriptions of his music, not a rigid official classification.

artist.biography: Chelsea Cutler is an American singer-songwriter and producer associated with Westport, Connecticut. Her solo catalogue blends intimate songwriting with elements of electronic pop, an editorial description of the way her releases have developed across several years. She emerged with early releases including 'Your Shirt' and the 2017 'Snow in October' project, then built a larger audience through the 'Sleeping with Roses' releases. Her first full-length album, 'How to Be Human,' arrived in 2020 and was followed by 'When I Close My Eyes' in 2021. She has also worked with Jeremy Zucker, a collaboration that sits alongside rather than replacing her solo work. The 2023 album 'Stellaria' marked an especially reflective chapter. In an interview with the Recording Academy, Cutler described valuing presence, openness, and vulnerability during its creation. She explained that 'you're all i ever dreamed of' revisited the early, delicate period of a personal relationship, while 'Your Bones' came from a melody that arrived unexpectedly in a voice note. In September 2026 she released 'IS THIS THE END?', extending her discography. For Afterglow, she offers a bridge from softer emotional pop toward understated electronic and singer-songwriter production. Mood and genre labels here are editorial navigation aids, not universally defined categories.

artist.short_description: Swedish songwriter whose intimate breakup narratives move between bright Scandinavian pop and country-tinged reflection.
artist.biography: Clara Mae is a Swedish singer-songwriter associated with Gävle, where she studied jazz singing and piano before pursuing music professionally in Stockholm. She developed her craft writing for other performers, with credits connected to dance-pop artists including David Guetta and Tiësto. Her collaboration with Norwegian electronic duo KREAM brought her voice to the 2016 track ‘Taped Up Heart,’ an early international breakthrough. She subsequently signed with Big Beat Records and established a solo identity built around candid relationship stories. Her 2018 six-song project ‘Sorry for Writing All the Songs About You,’ co-written with Cassandra Ströberg, follows the emotional arc of a romance, from early excitement to separation and acceptance. In a contemporary interview, Clara Mae explained that writing the songs helped her work through experiences from past relationships. Her 2020 collection ‘Drunk On Emotions’ continued that emotional focus and featured collaborations with gnash and country singer Russell Dickerson. The standalone 2021 single ‘Not Sad Anymore’ offered a different perspective: rediscovering independence after heartbreak. On the 2026 album ‘My Roots,’ her music moved toward a softer, more organic palette with country influences. Across those chapters, Clara Mae has emphasized story-led songwriting, melodic accessibility, and emotional specificity. For Afterglow listeners, her catalogue offers a bridge between polished Scandinavian pop, reflective breakup songs, and country-tinged singer-songwriter music.

artist.place_of_origin: Sweden (rural upbringing; specific town not independently verified)
artist.short_description: Swedish singer-songwriter whose reflective pop and folk-influenced songs focus on change, empathy and emotional resilience.
artist.biography: Elina is a Swedish singer-songwriter whose expanded name, Elina Gunhild Stridh, appears in the MusicBrainz catalogue. Before launching a performing career, she developed credits writing for other artists, including NEIKED, Zara Larsson and Astrid S. She began releasing her own music in 2018 with 'Wild Enough,' which she explained in a contemporary interview as a song about self-doubt and the need to believe in her abilities. Her first EP, 'In Hindsight,' appeared in 2019, followed by 'Remember' in 2020. The latter project is especially valuable for listeners interested in the stories behind songs: Elina provided an original track-by-track account to American Songwriter. She described 'Free' as reflecting on the difficulty of leaving a relationship while searching for happiness, 'Another Round' as the temptation to romanticize the past, and 'Paper Planes' as loving people enough to accept their separation. The title song, 'Remember,' offered reassurance to a loved one experiencing pain. In 2023 she released her debut album 'Whatever Happens Now,' preceded by 'Apologize,' which introduced a more folk-influenced direction and addressed growth after letting go. Her releases in 2025 further expanded the catalogue. Afterglow’s emotional-pop categorization reflects these lyrical connections; it is an editorial recommendation framework, not a rigid genre designation.

artist.place_of_origin: Virginia, United States (early upbringing); western North Carolina (adolescence); Nashville, Tennessee (based)
artist.short_description: Nashville-based singer-songwriter and producer John-Luke Carter, whose Mokita project blends vulnerable pop writing with electronic and acoustic elements.
artist.biography: Mokita is the artist project of John-Luke Carter, an American singer-songwriter and producer based in Nashville, Tennessee. According to a 2026 profile by his distributor, Carter was originally from Virginia and moved to North Carolina as a teenager. He described growing up with classical piano training, teaching himself guitar, and turning toward production after moving to Nashville to write songs. Alongside his solo music, he has worked behind the scenes as a songwriter and producer for other performers. Early Mokita releases leaned toward electronic pop, but later material has made room for acoustic instruments and a more restrained presentation. 'Love Alone' arrived in 2018, and Carter explained in a contemporary interview that it was motivated by the fear of being vulnerable in a relationship. The 2019 song 'colorblind' drew attention for addressing depression and the challenge of communicating an internal experience to someone else. Later projects include the 2022 EP 'Color Me In,' a self-titled 2025 album, and the 2026 single 'easy come, easy go.' His distributor characterized the later single as concerned with timing and emotional clarity. On Afterglow, Mokita offers a route from confessional songwriting into understated electronic pop. Those cross-genre recommendations are editorial choices rather than claims made by Carter himself.

artist.biography: Rosie Darling is the performing name of Rosemary Darling, a singer-songwriter born in Boston and based in Los Angeles. In a 2021 interview, she said that Rosie was already her everyday nickname, making it a natural stage name. Her early independent songs led to the release of 'Coping' in 2020, followed by the six-track 'Coping' EP in 2021. Discussing the project, Darling emphasized its grounding in the complicated emotions that accompany romance, friendship, heartbreak, and loneliness. Her songwriting is personal, but she has also spoken about wanting listeners to locate their own experiences inside the songs. The 2022 'Golden Age' EP expanded her storytelling. In a track-by-track interview she connected its title song to grief, isolation, and emotional upheaval during the pandemic, while 'Always Almost' explored the idea of someone who got away. Her debut album 'Lanterns' arrived in 2023 through Nettwerk. In subsequent interviews she characterized that collection as a challenging process of unpacking painful experiences and described 'Boxes' as particularly important to her recovery. For Afterglow, Darling provides an intimate link between soft heartbreak pop and reflective coming-of-age songwriting. That last categorization is editorial, rather than a formal description supplied by the artist.

artist.short_description: Indiana-raised singer-songwriter known for personal, narrative-led pop about relationships, self-image and growing up.
artist.biography: Sara Kays is an American singer-songwriter from Carmel, Indiana, whose songs often explore vulnerable moments with a direct, diary-like approach. She began singing young and received a guitar from her mother, then spent much of her school years performing covers on the street and at local venues. As she became more interested in writing her own material, she moved to Nashville, where she developed an ongoing recording partnership with producer Steven Martinez. Her early work includes the 2018 project A House Too Big and the 2020 EP Camera Shy. Songs such as Smaller Than This, Chosen Last and No Matter the Season brought candid subjects, including self-image and isolation, into her music. Kays used short clips on TikTok to test unfinished ideas; the response to Remember That Night? encouraged her to complete and release it quickly in November 2020. That song became her breakthrough recording and led to wider touring and television exposure. In 2021, she released Struck By Lightning on Atlantic Records, including a duet with Cavetown. Her songwriting frequently returns to everyday relationships, friendship changes and the discomfort of growing up, while allowing personal experiences to shape the stories. In January 2025, Bench Sitter began a new release chapter, followed by the seven-song Reasons To Call You project in May. For Afterglow, her catalogue offers several entry points into intimate, narrative-led emotional pop.

artist.name: Sasha Alex Sloan
artist.short_description: Boston-born singer-songwriter known for intimate pop that explores relationships, family, self-image, and the discomforts of growing up.
artist.biography: Sasha Alex Sloan is an American singer-songwriter from the Boston area who records under a name different from the expanded name Alexandra Artourovna Yatchenko listed in AllMusic. In a 2020 interview, Sloan described learning piano as a child, writing early songs, and eventually moving to Los Angeles after signing a songwriting publishing deal. She first developed her career writing with and for other artists before releasing her own material. The 2019 single 'Dancing With Your Ghost' brought wider attention to her reflective style; Sloan has explained that its concept arose after a close family friend lost her husband. Her 2020 debut album 'Only Child' pushed beyond conventional breakup songs into upbringing, family, vulnerability, body image, and existential questions. She supplied Apple Music with detailed, first-person commentary about the album, including how 'House With No Mirrors' came from a difficult moment involving her self-image and how 'Until It Happens to You' addresses the inability to comfort someone facing loss. In later years Sloan released 'I Blame the World' in 2022 and 'Me Again' in 2024, broadening a catalogue still strongly associated with unguarded writing. Afterglow groups her with emotional and confessional pop as an editorial classification rather than a claim about a single official genre.

artist.short_description: Swedish singer-songwriter whose emotionally candid pop blends polished hooks, personal storytelling, and collaborations with electronic producers.
artist.biography:
SHY Martin is the performing name of Sara Hjellström, a Swedish singer-songwriter raised in Lerdala, a small town in southern Sweden. She began making music at a young age, playing guitar and joining a band before studying songwriting at Musikmakarna in northern Sweden. Her career developed first behind the scenes: she co-wrote and performed on Mike Perry’s 2016 single “The Ocean” and contributed to songs associated with The Chainsmokers and other international pop artists.

Her own releases took shape in the late 2010s. The EP “Overthinking” arrived in 2018, followed by “Sad Songs” in 2020. In a first-person track-by-track account of “Sad Songs,” she described material drawn from broken relationships, the loss of friendship and her experiences with anxiety. The EP balances confessional subjects with polished pop songwriting.

After stepping back from a broader industry-writing routine, she returned with “wish I didn’t know you” in 2022, describing that bedroom-written song as a way back to enjoying music-making. Her debut full-length album, “late night thoughts,” followed in May 2023. In interviews, she characterized the album as a more personal project exploring emotional strain and other experiences she had previously struggled to address. The result spans intimate songwriting and accessible contemporary pop without reducing her work to a single mood.
